<a name="OpenCodeConfigDir"></a>OpenCode's home\-relative configuration paths and the plugin filenames Takt deploys into its plugin directory.

```go
const (
    // OpenCodeConfigDir is OpenCode's configuration directory under home.
    OpenCodeConfigDir = ".config/opencode"
    // OpenCodeConfigFile is OpenCode's configuration filename.
    OpenCodeConfigFile = "opencode.json"
    // OpenCodeConfigRelativePath is the slash-separated manifest path owned by OpenCode.
    OpenCodeConfigRelativePath = OpenCodeConfigDir + "/" + OpenCodeConfigFile
    // OpenCodeCLIConfigFile is the terminal client's configuration filename.
    OpenCodeCLIConfigFile = "cli.json"
    // OpenCodeCLIConfigRelativePath is the slash-separated manifest path of the terminal client configuration.
    OpenCodeCLIConfigRelativePath = OpenCodeConfigDir + "/" + OpenCodeCLIConfigFile
    // OpenCodeSkillsDir is the home-relative directory OpenCode V2 loads skills from.
    OpenCodeSkillsDir = ".opencode/skills"

    // ArchifySkillID is the upstream Archify skill directory name OpenCode discovers.
    ArchifySkillID = "archify"
    // ArchifySkillRelDir is the home-relative slash path of the installed Archify skill.
    ArchifySkillRelDir = OpenCodeSkillsDir + "/" + ArchifySkillID
    // ArchifyBinaryRelPath is the home-relative slash path of Archify's Node CLI entrypoint.
    ArchifyBinaryRelPath = ArchifySkillRelDir + "/bin/archify.mjs"
    // ArchifyManagedMarkerKey is the receipt Takt writes into the Archify tree it
    // extracts, tracked in the ownership manifest for a Takt-managed install.
    ArchifyManagedMarkerKey = ArchifySkillRelDir + "/.takt-receipt"
    // ArchifyRetiredRelDir is the home-relative slash path a deselected managed
    // Archify tree moves to before removal, outside the skills OpenCode loads,
    // so an interrupted removal is finished later without touching the skill path.
    ArchifyRetiredRelDir = StateDirName + "/archify-retired"

    // OpenCodePluginsDir is the directory OpenCode loads plugins from.
    OpenCodePluginsDir = "plugins"
    // VFSPluginFile is the deployed governed-VFS plugin filename.
    VFSPluginFile = "takt-vfs.ts"
)
```

<a name="EnvSandboxAllowedDomains"></a>EnvSandboxAllowedDomains names the environment variable with which the user opts shell sandboxes into a network allowlist: comma\-separated domain patterns such as "github.com,\*.npmjs.org". Unset or empty leaves the network unrestricted; Takt imposes no domain of its own.

```go
const EnvSandboxAllowedDomains = "TAKT_SANDBOX_ALLOWED_DOMAINS"
```

```go

```

```go

```

<a name="MemoryServerKey"></a>MemoryServerKey is the MCP server key clients register the memory service under; it is distinctive so it never replaces or collides with a user's server under a generic key such as "memory".

```go
const MemoryServerKey = "takt_memory"
```

<a name="StateDirName"></a>StateDirName is the workspace\-local state directory shared across Takt components.

```go
const StateDirName = ".takt-ai"
```

<a name="ComponentID"></a>
## type ComponentID

ComponentID names an installable piece so setup and lifecycle can select parts without string guessing.

```go
type ComponentID string
```

<a name="ComponentSkills"></a>Component IDs are the closed set of independently installable pieces.

```go
const (
    // ComponentSkills names the skills piece so installs can toggle skills independently.
    ComponentSkills ComponentID = "skills"
    // ComponentContext7 names the docs-lookup integration so installs can toggle it independently.
    ComponentContext7 ComponentID = "context7"
    // ComponentCodegraph names the codebase-exploration MCP integration, mandatory core.
    ComponentCodegraph ComponentID = "codegraph"
    // ComponentArchify names the optional Archify diagramming and codebase-analysis integration.
    ComponentArchify ComponentID = "archify"
)
```

<a name="GitPermissionRule"></a>
## type GitPermissionRule

GitPermissionRule is one native shell permission over a Git command pattern, where "\*" matches any text.

```go
type GitPermissionRule struct {
    Pattern string
    Effect  string
}
```

<a name="GitPermissionRules"></a>
### func GitPermissionRules

```go
func GitPermissionRules(role RoleClass) []GitPermissionRule
```

GitPermissionRules is role's Git policy as native shell permission patterns, in evaluation order for a host where the last matching rule wins. Every role but the orchestrator denies every git command, then allows each read\-only subcommand, and a read\-only subcommand carrying one of its writing options returns to the deny; a form the patterns cannot tell apart from a mutation keeps the deny. The orchestrator allows git and asks only for the actions in orchestratorGatedGit, for an amended commit and for a hard reset \(PR\-VFS\-GIT\-5\); every other Git mutation, a plain local commit included, is its conduct.

<a name="InjectionResult"></a>
## type InjectionResult

InjectionResult reports what an inject or remove changed so callers can record ownership and show honest summaries.

```go
type InjectionResult struct {
    // Changed flags whether any file changed, so callers can skip redundant bookkeeping.
    Changed bool
    // Files lists touched paths, so ownership and summaries stay accurate.
    Files []string
    // Preserved lists paths left for the user, so kept content is never reported as managed.
    Preserved []string
}
```

<a name="ModelAssignment"></a>
## type ModelAssignment

ModelAssignment pairs one model with its effort so each sub\-agent has a single clear runtime choice.

```go
type ModelAssignment struct {
    // Model holds the target-specific model id, explicit so typos fail fast instead of silently defaulting.
    Model string // target-specific model identifier
    // Effort holds the effort level; empty means target default, so callers can omit what they do not tune.
    Effort string // "" = target default; "low" | "medium" | "high"
}
```

<a name="RoleClass"></a>
## type RoleClass

RoleClass names one fixed permission profile so every specialist gets exactly the access it needs.

```go
type RoleClass string
```

<a name="RoleOrchestrator"></a>Role classes are the closed set of permission profiles.

```go
const (
    // RoleOrchestrator names the dispatch owner, the only role with git-write rights so history stays controlled.
    RoleOrchestrator RoleClass = "orchestrator"
    // RoleDirectInterlocutor names the user-facing role, the only voice allowed to hold the conversation.
    RoleDirectInterlocutor RoleClass = "direct_interlocutor"
    // RolePlanningAuthor names the spec and design author, separate so plans stay reviewable before execution.
    RolePlanningAuthor RoleClass = "planning_author"
    // RoleExecution names the contract implementer, fenced to file work so builds stay reproducible.
    RoleExecution RoleClass = "execution"
    // RoleVerification names the evidence judge, internal so verdicts stay independent of user chat.
    RoleVerification RoleClass = "verification"
    // RoleQualityAssurance names the product critic (mutation, exploration, non-functional analysis), internal and read-only over the project so its findings stay independent of the code it critiques.
    RoleQualityAssurance RoleClass = "quality_assurance"
    // RoleMaintenance names the harness-controlled cycle runner (GC, dreaming), never invocable as an interlocutor.
    RoleMaintenance RoleClass = "maintenance"
)
```

<a name="VFSCapability"></a>
## type VFSCapability

VFSCapability names one VFS operation that an agent instance may use. Instances with no VFS access declare an explicit empty capability list.

```go
type VFSCapability string
```

<a name="VFSCapabilityClaimList"></a>

```go
const (
    // VFSCapabilityClaimList lets the orchestrator list claims.
    VFSCapabilityClaimList VFSCapability = "claim_list"
    // VFSCapabilityClaimAssign lets the orchestrator assign claims.
    VFSCapabilityClaimAssign VFSCapability = "claim_assign"
    // VFSCapabilityClaimRelease lets the orchestrator release claims.
    VFSCapabilityClaimRelease VFSCapability = "claim_release"
    // VFSCapabilityBind lets an instance establish a VFS binding.
    VFSCapabilityBind VFSCapability = "bind"
    // VFSCapabilityWrite lets an instance stage file writes.
    VFSCapabilityWrite VFSCapability = "write"
    // VFSCapabilityRead lets an instance read workspace or staged content.
    VFSCapabilityRead VFSCapability = "read"
    // VFSCapabilityDelete lets an instance stage file deletions.
    VFSCapabilityDelete VFSCapability = "delete"
    // VFSCapabilityDiscard lets the orchestrator discard an author's staged changes.
    VFSCapabilityDiscard VFSCapability = "discard"
    // VFSCapabilityVerify lets an instance verify another instance's delta.
    VFSCapabilityVerify VFSCapability = "verify"
    // VFSCapabilityConsolidate lets the orchestrator consolidate verified work.
    VFSCapabilityConsolidate VFSCapability = "consolidate"
    // VFSCapabilityInspect lets an instance read the recorded journal and
    // execution history, which hold no file content.
    VFSCapabilityInspect VFSCapability = "inspect"
)
```

<a name="VFSCapability.Valid"></a>
### func \(VFSCapability\) Valid

```go
func (c VFSCapability) Valid() bool
```

Valid reports whether c names one of the closed set of VFS operations.
